subject: Order Form: tiered packaging & pricing exhibits — redline questions
messages:
From: Elena Park <elena@hyphaanalytics.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: procurement@hyphaanalytics.com
Date: 2027-08-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Order form + pricing exhibits — initial redlines and clarifying questions

Hi Jonas,

Thanks for sending over the updated order form and exhibits. Procurement ran a quick redline pass and attached two files (Hypha_OrderForm_v2_redlines.docx, Pricing_Exhibit_Tiers.pdf). Before we escalate to our legal team, we need clarification on a few pricing/packaging points that are ambiguous on our side:

1) Anchoring / floor & cap triggers: Section 2.3 references an "anchoring" mechanism that recalibrates the fee band if monthly usage falls below the "floor" for two consecutive months. Can you confirm how "monthly usage" is measured (tokens consumed vs. API calls vs. billed units)? We need explicit measurement language (start-of-month snapshot? rolling 30-day?).

2) Tiered packaging definitions: Exhibit A lists SKU bands (Tier 1, Tier 2, Tier 3) but the spacing/aggregation for multi-product bundles is unclear — e.g., do embeddings and text-generation credits combine toward the same band? Procurement wants a clear formula.

3) True-up / annualization: The doc references a "12-month annualized commit" but the reconciliation timing isn't specified. Our finance team expects a 30-day true-up window following quarter close, not a 90-day backlog.

4) Price protection / stabilizer: There's a "stabilization carveout" that appears to permit a one-time repricing for a large negative demand delta. Is that intended to be unilateral? If so, we need a cap on the adjustment and notification timing.

5) Onboarding credit & Surcharges: We noticed a short paragraph about a "stabilization surcharge" for customers who opt into price protection. Can you confirm how that surcharge is calculated and whether it applies retroactively?

High level, our legal prefers redline language that points at deterministic, measurable triggers (e.g., "monthly billable units measured as sum of tokens consumed across all models in the billing account, with 30-day rolling average"), and explicit cure periods for any repricing.

Would you be open to a short call tomorrow to walk through each item? If you can, please also send the team's recommended draft language for the anchoring and true-up clauses so we can circulate internally.

Best,
Elena
Elena Park
Head of Procurement, Hypha Analytics

Attachments: Hypha_OrderForm_v2_redlines.docx (docx), Pricing_Exhibit_Tiers.pdf (pdf)

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Park <elena@hyphaanalytics.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com, karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com, lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2027-08-01T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Order form + pricing exhibits — initial redlines and clarifying questions

Elena — thanks for the detailed pass and the redlines. Looping in Marissa (pricing/legal liaison), Karthik (contracts) and Lauren (finance) to help close these out. Quick answers and proposed draft language below — see also the attached draft that highlights the samples in the order form.

1) Measurement (anchoring floor/cap): Proposed language: "Monthly billable units means the sum of billed tokens consumed across all model endpoints on the Customer billing account during the calendar month, measured using Redwood's production metering (UTC). A rolling 30-day average will be used to determine consecutive month triggers for the floor mechanism."

2) Tier aggregation: Proposed: "For multi-product bundles, billable units from embedding and generation endpoints are aggregated under a single billing account and count toward tier thresholds on a tokens-equivalent basis; Appendix A includes conversion factors for embeddings -> token equivalence." (we attach a sample conversion table).

3) True-up timing: Proposed: "Quarterly reconciliations will occur within 30 calendar days following quarter end. Any underage/overage will be invoiced/credited on the next monthly invoice."

4) Stabilization carveout: We're happy to narrow the language. Proposed: "Redwood may propose a temporary repricing only if Customer's monthly billable units decline by more than 60% versus prior-quarter monthly average, subject to a 45-day notice and a cap on repricing equal to 20% of base fees, unless mutually agreed otherwise."

5) Surcharge: Proposed: "Any price-protection surcharge, if elected, will be stated up-front in Exhibit B and will not be applied retroactively to invoices already issued; surcharge calculation is defined as X% of base monthly fee and will be displayed on invoice line Items."

Action items:
- Marissa / Karthik: please review the precise statutory phrasing for 1 & 4 and mark any legal objections in-track.
- Elena: if the above looks close, can we confirm whether a 20% cap on repricing is acceptable or if Hypha will require a different cap?

I can be on a call tomorrow 10:00–10:30 PT or 14:00–14:30 PT.

Cheers,
Jonas
Jonas Weber
Head of Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference

Attachments: Redwood_Draft_Language_1-5.docx (docx)"

From: Elena Park <elena@hyphaanalytics.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: procurement@hyphaanalytics.com
Date: 2027-08-02T08:46:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Order form + pricing exhibits — initial redlines and clarifying questions

Jonas — thanks for the quick turnaround and the concrete phrasing. A few inline responses:

> 1) Measurement (anchoring floor/cap): Proposed language...
We like the rolling 30-day average, but procurement insists on an optional "start-of-month snapshot" if we opt into forecasted commitments (our FP&A needs deterministic anchors for budgeting). Can you add an alternate measurement sentence that allows a monthly snapshot by mutual agreement?

> 2) Tier aggregation: Proposed: "...tokens-equivalent basis; Appendix A includes conversion factors..."
Acceptable — please include the conversion table as a labeled appendix in the final order form.

> 3) True-up timing: Proposed: 30 calendar days following quarter end
Accepted by finance. Please ensure invoices reflect credits within that window.

> 4) Stabilization carveout: Proposed 60% decline trigger / 45-day notice / 20% cap
Our legal is comfortable with a carveout but asks that the repricing cap be tied to a formula rather than a fixed percentage (e.g., "no more than the lesser of 20% of base fees or the difference between prior-quarter and current-quarter billable units amortized over N months"). Can Redwood propose workable amortization months?

> 5) Surcharge: Proposed language...
We will accept a surcharge if it is non-retroactive and capped, with clear invoice labeling.

Procurement is also pushing for a one-time onboarding credit if we can agree to a 12-month annualized commit. If Redwood is willing to provide a $25k onboarding credit, we'll accept a modest fee-surcharge formula and move to legal redlines.

We can do the call tomorrow at 10:00 PT.

Best,
Elena

Date: 2027-08-03T15:23:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Order form + pricing exhibits — initial redlines and clarifying questions

Elena / team — appreciate the constructive notes. From a commercial/legal balance perspective, Redwood can accept the following compromise:

• Measurement: Keep rolling 30-day average as default; add optional clause: "By mutual written agreement, Customer and Redwood may elect to adopt a start-of-month snapshot for committed accounts; such election must be documented in Appendix C."

• Repricing cap: We will adopt a formulaic cap: "The repricing shall not exceed the lesser of (i) 20% of the base monthly fee or (ii) the prorated difference between prior-quarter billable units and current-quarter billable units amortized over three months." (we propose 3 months amortization; open to 6 if Hypha requests).

• Onboarding credit: Redwood agrees to a one-time onboarding credit of $25,000 tied to execution of a 12-month annualized commit at the agreed bands. Credit will be applied on first invoice post-execution.

• Surcharge: Will be non-retroactive and displayed as a separate invoice line; calculation formula will be included in Exhibit B.

Next steps:
1) Jonas — please update the order form with the Appendix C snapshot election language and the repricing formula above.
2) Karthik / Legal — please review the exact statutory phrasing and confirm the 3-month amortization is defensible; if not, propose 6 months.
3) Elena — if Hypha accepts this compromise, we'll produce a clean redline and a final DocuSign envelope by EOD Friday.

I'll be on the call at 10:00 PT tomorrow with Karthik.

Thanks,
Marissa
Director, Commercial Contracts | Redwood Inference

Attachments: Revised_Compromise_Summary.pdf (pdf)
